questions.stem: As x gets very large, what happens to f(x) = 1/x?
questions.explain: Dividing 1 by a huge number gives a tiny positive number, so the graph flattens toward 0 without ever reaching it.

questions.stem: A linear model uses weights w = (3, −2, 1). What does it predict, w·x, for x = (2, 1, 4)?
A model has a training error of 2% and a validation error of 25%. What does this suggest?
questions.explain: A tiny training error with a much larger validation error means the model memorised the training data. That is high variance.
